UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010; Real Decreto 95/2024, de 30 de enero, por el que se regulan los registros de titularidad real; Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD5) as transposed into Spanish law.
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

A virtual office or serviced address is permitted for an SL only if it provides a physical premises in Spain where legal notifications can be received, statutory books are maintained, and supervisory authorities can inspect activities. For the ISIC 4669 wholesale petrochemical trading scope (AML Medium-Risk Enhanced), a pure virtual mailbox is inadvisable; a dedicated serviced office with management presence and documentation storage is the minimum acceptable commercial substance.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry, for the negative name certificate) and Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Commercial Registry) of the province of the registered office.

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Spanish Capital Companies Act), Articles 4, 19-27 and 62-66; Law 18/2022 'Crea y Crece' (Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva regime); Real Decreto 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil); Ley 14/2013 and Real Decreto 1270/2003 (notarial and registry fee schedules).

Formation / constitutional filings

Public deed of incorporation (Escritura de Constitución) signed before a Notary and inscribed in the Mercantile Registry, together with the AEAT tax form Modelo 600 for stamp duty (AJ).

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 70 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

The share capital must be fully subscribed and paid in at constitution. Standard SL minimum paid-up capital is EUR 3,000; under the Law 18/2022 Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva regime the minimum may be reduced to EUR 1, with restrictions on dividend distribution and profit application until the EUR 3,000 threshold is reached. Capital is evidenced by a Spanish bank deposit certificate (certificado de desembolso); no statutory escrow account is required.

Funding & unlock path: Fire safety certification of the industrial warehouse under Real Decreto 2267/2004 (Reglamento de Seguridad contra Incendios en Establecimientos Industriales) and the CTE DB-SI building code; structural load validation of floors and racking systems under CTE DB-SE; workplace health and safety clearance under Ley 31/1995 and Real Decreto 486/1997 covering evacuation routes, lighting, climate, sanitation, first-aid facilities, and emergency plans; all permissions must be recorded in the company's official workplace inspection documentation.

Paid-in capital rule: The share capital must be fully subscribed and paid in at constitution. Standard SL minimum paid-up capital is EUR 3,000; under the Law 18/2022 Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva regime the minimum may be reduced to EUR 1, with restrictions on dividend distribution and profit application until the EUR 3,000 threshold is reached. Capital is evidenced by a Spanish bank deposit certificate (certificado de desembolso); no statutory escrow account is required.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
RESOLVED: (1) That the subscribed share capital, fully paid in and evidenced by the bank deposit certificate, is duly accepted, and each founding member's shareholding is approved as recorded in the deed. (2) That the registered office of the company is adopted at [address], within the municipality of [city], Spain. (3) That the following persons are appointed to the joint office of administrator(s): [Name(s)], accepting the office and acknowledging the powers conferred. (4) That the administration is authorized to open national bank accounts and to transact LC financing operations, to execute all supplementary notarial and registry deeds, and to apply for the company's CIF/NIF and municipal operating licenses.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Mandatory Environmental Clearance

Ministerio de Industria, Comercio y Turismo (General Directorate of Industry) for industrial establishment registration; autonomous community industry service (Consejería de Industria / Dirección General de Industria, Energía y Minas); and the municipal Ayuntamiento for the activity and opening license.

Category: Licencia de actividad y apertura de establecimiento (municipal operating and opening license for a commercial wholesale warehouse); alternatively, Declaración Responsable de inicio de actividad for premises classified as innocuous or without significant environmental impact.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), official portal at www.agenciatributaria.es

E-government filing portal

Spanish resident entities obtain NIF at incorporation via the Mercantile Registry. Non-resident entities procure NIF through AEAT by submitting form 036 or online registration for tax purposes, followed by tax identification number issuance.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — Spanish resident entities obtain NIF at incorporation via the Mercantile Registry. Non-resident entities procure NIF through AEAT by submitting form 036 or online registration for tax purposes, followed by tax identification number issuance.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation

Available election forms

No US-style check-the-box elections available. Spain applies entity-level taxation with territorial scope for certain income categories and hybrid mismatch adjustments under the Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD).

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

1,000,000 EUR

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

0% VAT rate applies to exports of goods and services to non-EU customers. Eligibility requires proof that the goods are exported outside the EU or services rendered to non-residents, with supporting documentation.

  • Customs Export Declaration (ED)
  • Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document
  • Inward Remittance Certificate or proof of payment

Mandatory implementation of Facturae electronic invoicing system requiring digital stamps (sello electrónico) for all VAT-liable invoices. Large taxpayers must comply with real-time reporting and API integration with AEAT systems for clearance and stamping.

Fraudulent claims of zero-rating on exports result in penalties of up to 100% of the evaded VAT plus interest. Retrospective clawback applies if export documentation is insufficient or false, with potential criminal prosecution for intentional fraud.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

The euro is fully convertible, and Spain applies no exchange-control restrictions on either current-account flows (trade settlement, service fees, dividends, interest, royalties) or capital-account operations (equity injections, intra-group loans, securities, acquisitions) with EU/EEA counterparties under Article 63 TFEU. For third countries, Law 19/2003 maintains unrestricted movement of capital subject only to: (i) statistical declaration obligations to Banco de España under Circular 4/2023; (ii) EU/CFSP restrictive measures and sanctions screening; (iii) anti-money-laundering verification under Law 10/2010; and (iv) foreign-investment screening under Regulation (EU) 2019/452 for investments affecting security, critical infrastructure, or sensitive technology. Non-resident profit remittance by an SL shareholder is free of FX approval; the only practical hurdles are corporate tax certification (dividend withholding at 19% where applicable, plus Form 210/211 filing) and the bank's internal compliance sign-off. Multi-currency accounts (EUR, USD, CNY, MXN, BRL) may be opened freely, and trade invoices may be denominated in any currency.

Export proceeds surrender rules

No statutory surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio apply in Spain. The SL may retain 100% of export proceeds in EUR or in foreign currency and may dispose of them freely. The only obligations are statistical: banks aggregate and file BE-1 transaction declarations on behalf of clients, while clients must directly file BE-2 declarations to Banco de España for individual cross-border transactions exceeding the quantitative thresholds set in Circular 4/2023, and BE-3 position declarations for foreign-currency and external assets/liabilities balances. No 30-day conversion window, no repatriation quota, and no Central Bank approval is required for polymer export settlements.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting as the central monetary authority and competent statistical authority for external transactions, jointly with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones of the Secretaría de Estado de Comercio (Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business), which operates the Foreign Investment Registry and the capital-movement control framework under Law 19/2003 of 4 July 2003 and Royal Decree 571/2023.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Feasibility rating: MEDIUM as an ancillary payment rail and LOW as the primary cross-border treasury rail for this ISIC 4669 wholesale business. Spanish e-money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions regulated under Law 21/2011 and PSD2 (transposed by Royal Decree-Law 19/2018) may lawfully open and operate payment accounts, process SWIFT/SEPA transfers, and provide FX conversion; however, they cannot extend credit, open or negotiate commercial letters of credit, issue guarantees, or act as correspondent banks for documentary collections. An SL executing bulk petrochemical polymer trade must therefore maintain its irrevocable LC and settlement infrastructure at a licensed credit institution. Offshore EMIs (e.g., post-Brexit UK payment firms) have lost EU passporting and require a Spanish branch authorization from Banco de España; reliance on such providers alone would be incompatible with the target payment rails and would trigger bank de-risking responses.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Payment flows to or from high-risk or embargoed jurisdictions (e.g., certain Latin American, Middle Eastern, or African polymer suppliers) generating sanctions or PEP-list hits.

Root cause: Payment flows to or from high-risk or embargoed jurisdictions (e.g., certain Latin American, Middle Eastern, or African polymer suppliers) generating sanctions or PEP-list hits.

Defense evidence: EU Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN and UN Security Council screening certificates; complete counterparty KYC packs; Incoterms 2020 purchase/sale contracts; UCP 600-compliant letters of credit and bills of lading/CMR waybills; EUR1/end-use certificates confirming non-dual-use bulk plastics; customs entry summary declarations (EORI-linked).
Opaque beneficial-ownership chain or a non-resident ultimate shareholder unable to demonstrate the source of funds used for the capital injection.

Root cause: Opaque beneficial-ownership chain or a non-resident ultimate shareholder unable to demonstrate the source of funds used for the capital injection.

Defense evidence: Apostilled and sworn-translated certificate of incorporation and registry abstracts of each intermediate shareholder; statutory beneficial-owner declarations filed under Law 10/2010; the SL's Libro Registro de Socios; source-of-funds evidence (12-month bank statements, audited parent-company financial statements, share-acquisition deed proving origin of capital).
Triangular trade pattern: invoices and settlements moving through third countries inconsistent with the stated physical supply chain, or abrupt high-turnover spikes.

Root cause: Triangular trade pattern: invoices and settlements moving through third countries inconsistent with the stated physical supply chain, or abrupt high-turnover spikes.

Defense evidence: 18-month treasury and liquidity projection; full trade-cycle narrative (order, LC issuance, shipment, inspection, settlement); open-contract register; port receipts and warehouse storage documents; VAT/customs extracts (Modelo 303, Single Administrative Document) showing physical goods movement; audited annual accounts for the SL.
Absence of economic substance in Spain: foreign-resident management, no local premises, and no payroll or social-security footprint in the jurisdiction.

Root cause: Absence of economic substance in Spain: foreign-resident management, no local premises, and no payroll or social-security footprint in the jurisdiction.

Defense evidence: Spanish substance file: execution of office lease, registration with Seguridad Social, local director passes NIE and tax registration, corporate meeting minutes signed in Spain, designated tax representative for Hacienda, and the SL's valid CIF plus evidence of active VAT/payroll returns.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Compliant routing for the initial paid-in capital of the SL: SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident shareholder's account to the SL's EUR IBAN (TARGET2/SEPA interoperable). Field 50a must identify the remitting shareholder; field 70 (Remittance Information) must state 'Aporte de capital social — suscripción de participaciones' followed by the public-deed number and date; field 72 should reference the notarial authorization. If the funds are deposited before incorporation, they must be placed in a blocked escrow deposit account certified by the bank (Certificado de Depósito) addressed to the notary. The verification package comprises: notarial deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución), share-subscription list (lista de suscripción), capital-payment certificate, and notary's declaration of compliance with Law 14/2013. Concurrently, the SL must file the declaración de inversión exterior with the Foreign Investment Registry under Law 19/2003 and Royal Decree 571/2023 within the statutory filing window, using the official DIA (Declaración Informativa de Inversión Exterior) form including the purpose code 1110 (investment by non-residents in shares of a Spanish limited company). The receiving bank mirrors the transaction in its BE-2/4 statistical declarations. Shareholder loans must be documented as a separate 'participación financiera' transaction with a distinct concept to prevent re-characterization as hidden equity contributions.Primary clearing rails for bulk polyethylene and polypropylene purchases: (i) Irrevocable Documentary Letter of Credit governed by UCP 600, communicated via SWIFT MT700 (issue), MT707 (amendment), MT754 (advice) and settled through MT103/MT202 cover payments with MT400/MT412 reimbursement where applicable; (ii) Standby Letter of Credit (MT760) for supplier security margins; (iii) SWIFT MT103 for open-account and advance-payment disbursements to verified suppliers, using the correspondent clearing network of the issuing Spanish bank with the USD nostro chain; and (iv) SEPA Credit Transfers (SCT/XML ISO 20022) for low-value intra-EU settlements. For LatAm-bound flows, clearing through Banco Santander or BBVA correspondent networks reduces friction and permits same-day value. All outbound disbursements must carry the correct purpose classification for the Banco de España statistical declaration (purpose code 4200 for trade credits, 4300 for goods trade settlement), reference the commercial invoice and Incoterms delivery stage, and must be screened against the EU/OFAC/UN sanctions lists before initiation. Commercial LCs should be denominated in USD for Middle Eastern and Asian master-batch suppliers and in EUR for intra-EU counterparties, with swap-in-place hedging to match the SL's EUR base.Outright EUR/USD FX Forwards (physical delivery), typically 1-week to 12-month tenors, executed under an ISDA 2002 master agreement or the Spanish Contrato Marco de Operaciones Financieras (CMOF), with EMIR transaction reporting to a registered trade repository and no central-clearing obligation for vanilla foreign-exchange forwards.Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on restrictive LatAm and emerging-market currencies (e.g., Argentine peso, Venezuelan bolívar, Nigerian naira) referenced to EUR/USD, permitted for bona fide trade-hedging purposes, subject to EMIR reporting, Banco de España statistical declaration, and documented underlying exposure.Cross-Currency Swaps (EUR/USD fixed-for-fixed) aligned with the maturity profile of the import trade-finance book, negotiated under the bank's Credit Support Annex to cover principal and interest re-pricing risk on USD-denominated polymer inventory purchases.FX Swaps (swap de divisas) for periodic conversion and reconversion of USD export receipts into EUR operating cash, permissible only where a continuous underlying trade-exposure schedule and the SL's treasury policy substantiate the transaction; transactions are reported to Banco de España under the BE statistical framework.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM as an ancillary payment rail and LOW as the primary cross-border treasury rail for this ISIC 4669 wholesale business. Spanish e-money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions regulated under Law 21/2011 and PSD2 (transposed by Royal Decree-Law 19/2018) may lawfully open and operate payment accounts, process SWIFT/SEPA transfers, and provide FX conversion; however, they cannot extend credit, open or negotiate commercial letters of credit, issue guarantees, or act as correspondent banks for documentary collections. An SL executing bulk petrochemical polymer trade must therefore maintain its irrevocable LC and settlement infrastructure at a licensed credit institution. Offshore EMIs (e.g., post-Brexit UK payment firms) have lost EU passporting and require a Spanish branch authorization from Banco de España; reliance on such providers alone would be incompatible with the target payment rails and would trigger bank de-risking responses.

Deposit of Annual Accounts (Cuentas Anuales) including auditor's report where mandatory and beneficial-owner identification sheet Within six months after the financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 30 June of the following year $60 USD Late deposit triggers a fine of EUR 1,200 to EUR 12,000, closure of the company's registry file, and blockage of registration of corporate acts; persistent non-filing can result in dissolution and eventual strike-off after liquidation.

Annual confirmation of Ultimate Beneficial Ownership data embedded in the deposited annual accounts Same deadline as the annual accounts deposit: within six months after the financial year-end $0 USD Incomplete or false UBO information triggers anti-money-laundering fines under Law 10/2010, registry closure, and rejection of annual accounts deposit.

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% Spanish non-resident withholding tax on dividends paid by a Spanish resident company, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. Dividends paid to a qualifying EU parent may be exempt under the Spanish implementation of the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, generally requiring at least a 5% participation or qualifying acquisition value, a minimum one-year holding period or commitment, subject-to-tax and legal-form conditions, and anti-abuse requirements.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

The return is filed within the 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year company ending on 31 December, the normal filing window is 1 to 25 July of the following year, subject to AEAT calendar adjustments and payment arrangements.

Deadline: · Frequency:

The normal filing windows are 1 to 20 April, 1 to 20 October, and 1 to 20 December. The exact period is adjusted when the final day is a non-business day. Large companies and taxpayers using the alternative tax-base method calculate instalments under the applicable statutory method.

Deadline: · Frequency:

Generally filed during the month following the ten-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the normal period is November.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Spanish transfer-pricing documentation is generally required for controlled transactions, subject to statutory exemptions. A principal exemption applies where the aggregate controlled transactions with the same related person or entity do not exceed EUR 250,000 at arm's length during the tax period, excluding specified transactions and subject to the documentation regulations. A local file is generally required for material controlled transactions; a master file is generally required for Spanish entities forming part of a group subject to the applicable country-by-country reporting framework, with simplified documentation rules for smaller groups. Modelo 232 has separate reporting thresholds, including the general EUR 250,000 counterparty threshold and specific thresholds for certain categories.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not operate a standalone jurisdiction-wide Economic Substance Regulations regime equivalent to the UAE or certain offshore jurisdictions. Economic substance remains material under Spanish transfer-pricing rules, the principal-purpose and anti-abuse rules, the general anti-avoidance rule, the anti-hybrid rules, controlled foreign company rules, EU Parent-Subsidiary and Interest-Royalties Directive anti-abuse provisions, beneficial-ownership analysis, and permanent-establishment principles. A Spanish SL distributing petrochemical products should maintain real management, personnel or outsourced operational capacity under effective control, premises or verifiable logistics capability, inventory and risk management, bank and accounting controls, commercially supportable contracts, and decision-making evidence. Empty conduit structures, circular financing, non-arm's-length margins, artificial royalty or interest charges, and unsupported management fees are high-risk.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax evasion and fraudulent corporate tax return

Statutory sanction: Criminal tax fraud generally carries imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine of one to six times the amount defrauded, together with restitution and loss of public subsidies or tax benefits. Aggravated cases, including fraud exceeding EUR 600,000, organized conduct, or use of interposed persons, may carry imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and a fine of two to six times the amount defrauded. Administrative assessments, interest, and penalties may apply separately where criminal prosecution is not pursued.

Director personal liability: Directors and de facto managers may incur criminal liability where they knowingly participate, authorize, facilitate, or fail to prevent the offense. They may face imprisonment, fines, civil restitution, disqualification from public office or benefits, and personal tax liability under Spanish General Tax Law derivative-liability provisions. Travel restrictions may be imposed by a court where legally justified; there is no automatic travel ban solely because a tax return is late.
Transfer-pricing manipulation and profit shifting

Statutory sanction: AEAT may make a primary adjustment, corresponding adjustment, secondary adjustment, deny deductions, assess withholding tax, charge late-payment interest, and impose transfer-pricing documentation or valuation penalties. Failure to provide documentation or providing materially false or incomplete documentation may attract penalties calculated by reference to data or adjusted amounts, subject to statutory caps and minimums.

Director personal liability: Directors may become jointly or subsidiarily liable for assessed tax, penalties, or collection costs where statutory negligence, collaboration, asset stripping, or enforcement-obstruction conditions are met. Criminal exposure may arise if the conduct also satisfies the tax-fraud threshold.
False invoices, VAT fraud, and carousel fraud

Statutory sanction: VAT assessments, denial of input credit, proportional penalties linked to the improperly deducted or unpaid VAT, interest, seizure, and possible criminal prosecution apply. Tax fraud exceeding the criminal threshold may result in imprisonment and fines; customs and excise sanctions may also apply where import declarations are false.

Director personal liability: Directors and responsible officers may face criminal liability, personal civil restitution, derivative tax liability, disqualification, and asset-seizure measures. Travel restrictions can be ordered in criminal proceedings where necessary to secure the process.
Withholding-tax failure and unlawful profit repatriation

Statutory sanction: The Spanish SL may be assessed for the unwithheld amount, late-payment interest, and withholding-related penalties. Treaty or EU relief may be denied, and anti-abuse rules may recharacterize the payment or recipient. Repeated or fraudulent non-withholding can create broader tax-fraud exposure.

Director personal liability: Directors may incur derivative liability where they caused or negligently permitted the failure, particularly during liquidation or asset distributions. Knowing participation in fraudulent repatriation may create criminal and civil liability.
Shell company, beneficial-owner concealment, or artificial substance

Statutory sanction: Authorities may deny treaty or EU exemptions, apply the general anti-abuse rule, recharacterize transactions, deny deductions, assess tax and interest, impose tax penalties, and refer conduct for criminal investigation where fraud thresholds are met. Corporate-law and insolvency consequences may also arise.

Director personal liability: Directors and de facto controllers may be liable for tax debts, damages to creditors, unlawful distributions, concealment, and criminal offenses. Courts may disregard separate legal personality in exceptional cases involving abuse, fraud, or creditor prejudice; imprisonment and judicial travel restrictions are possible only where criminal-law conditions are met.
AML, sanctions, and trade-control violations

Statutory sanction: Under Spanish anti-money-laundering law, serious and very serious infringements may produce public or private warnings, substantial monetary fines, management disqualification, publication measures, and possible suspension or withdrawal of authorization where applicable. Criminal money laundering may carry imprisonment generally from 6 months to 6 years, fines, confiscation, and enhanced sanctions for aggravated conduct. EU and Spanish sanctions breaches may generate administrative and criminal consequences.

Director personal liability: Directors, compliance officers, and responsible managers may be personally sanctioned or prosecuted for knowing participation, authorization, or serious supervisory failure. Confiscation, civil restitution, disqualification, asset freezing, and court-ordered travel restrictions may apply in criminal proceedings.
Customs, origin, and trade misclassification

Statutory sanction: Customs duties, import VAT, interest, seizure, administrative fines, loss of simplified customs procedures, and potential criminal customs fraud sanctions may apply. The company may also lose commercial or customs-authorized-operator privileges.

Director personal liability: Directors and customs representatives may incur civil and administrative liability and, for deliberate fraud, criminal liability, confiscation, disqualification, and restitution obligations.
Accounting, corporate-record, and statutory-filing failure

Statutory sanction: Administrative tax penalties, denial of deductions, presumptive assessments, audit extensions, accounting sanctions, potential commercial-registry consequences, and insolvency or creditor claims may arise. Destruction or falsification of records can become a criminal offense.

Director personal liability: Directors may face civil liability to the company and creditors, derivative tax liability, insolvency disqualification, restitution, and criminal liability for deliberate falsification or concealment. Travel bans are not automatic but may be ordered in insolvency or criminal proceedings where statutory conditions are satisfied.
